exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery of both twins, unplanned cesarean delivery of both twins, combined delivery)
cohort: 19,723 women with twin pregnancies where the first twin was in cephalic position, in the Netherlands between 2000-2012
finding: Compared to vaginal delivery of both twins, unplanned cesarean delivery of both twins was associated with a twofold increase in neonatal mortality, while combined delivery was associated with a sevenfold increase in perinatal mortality and a five-fold increase in asphyxia-related outcomes.
mod_finding: Unplanned cesarean delivery of both twins, compared to vaginal delivery, was associated with a twofold increase in neonatal mortality, while combined delivery was associated with a sevenfold increase in perinatal mortality and a five-fold increase in asphyxia-related outcomes.
